purpose: Record the bounded corrected-source re-extraction output for the C2-LT-B13 incontinence-associated dermatitis row after PubMed source-resolution replaced the mismatched PMID 26428404 with PMID 22193141.

scope.extractionLimit: This register records corrected source-context extraction only; it does not itself create reviewed artifacts or authorize model admission.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Incontinence-associated dermatitis: a comprehensive review and update.
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Blocks the original registered PMID 26428404 because it resolves to a chemistry/crystallography article, and replaces the source route with PMID 22193141, a PubMed-indexed review titled 'Incontinence-associated dermatitis: a comprehensive review and update.'
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: The corrected source is a 2012 review article with PubMed abstract access and a 2026 PubMed record revision date. Use it only as IAD review-background vocabulary and source-route correction pending independent fresh review; it is not a current clinical guideline or product-selection source.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports bounded source-context framing that IAD literature discusses epidemiology, etiology and pathophysiology, connects urinary or fecal incontinence to dermatitis as a complication, and identifies persistent knowledge gaps. It may name IAD as a moisture/skin-barrier continuity domain but cannot support individual care advice or calibrated risk.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include moisture-exposure, urinary-or-fecal-incontinence-context, perineal-skin-barrier-breakdown, dermatitis/skin-inflammation-burden, pain-or-discomfort-burden, infection-entry-risk and evidence-gap/currentness-boundary.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Human IAD review context involving urinary or fecal incontinence complications, perineal skin and clinical nursing/wound-ostomy-continence literature. It is not generalized to all dermatology, all chronic wounds, all incontinence care, individual prognosis or product choice.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: urinary or fecal incontinence can create moisture exposure and perineal skin compromise; IAD is framed as dermatitis with etiology and pathophysiology routes relevant to skin-boundary maintenance, pain/discomfort burden, infection-entry risk and care burden.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: The PubMed abstract states that research remained limited and additional studies were urgently needed. This is a review/consensus-derived source route, not a randomized effect estimate, current guideline, validated endpoint definition, individual risk model or product-comparison evidence.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as corrected source identity, IAD background vocabulary, candidate variable names and uncertainty boundary. Do not reuse for skin-care regimens, antifungal or anti-inflammatory use, product selection, wound-care decisions, dermatology diagnosis, clinical instructions, calibrated prediction, intervention ranking or individual advice.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade to background-only if independent fresh review finds the abstract too old or too recommendation-oriented for the domain claim seed.
Block artifact promotion if the row is used to endorse cleansing, moisturization, protectant, antifungal, containment, anti-inflammatory, product or care-regimen claims.
Block model use if the row is treated as calibrated effect-size evidence, current guideline evidence, individual-risk evidence or clinical-validity evidence.
Downgrade if no full-text or newer source can bind IAD endpoint variables, measurement definitions or currentness boundaries.

modelPosition.primaryLocation: C2 source-maintenance skin-boundary and moisture-exposure continuity route
modelPosition.admissibleUse: corrected source identity, IAD vocabulary and candidate endpoint variables pending independent fresh review

sourceEvidenceTrace.finding: PubMed identifies PMID 22193141 as the 2012 J Wound Ostomy Continence Nurs review 'Incontinence-associated dermatitis: a comprehensive review and update' with DOI 10.1097/WON.0b013e31823fe246.
NCBI ESummary confirms title, authors, journal, publication date, review publication type and DOI for PMID 22193141.
NCBI EFetch abstract states the review updates IAD research, discusses epidemiology, etiology and pathophysiology, and concludes that research remains limited and additional studies are needed.

extractedRows.nextAction: Send this corrected extraction output to independent fresh review; create bounded reviewed artifacts only if review confirms scope, currentness and prohibited-use boundaries.
